verdict.rationale: Unleash documents its own API keys for SDKs, Edge and "other tools and automation," and backend tokens are scoped to selected projects and a single environment. That is genuine first-party scoped credentialing, and RBAC supports custom roles. However, the evidence never shows how write-capable Admin API or MCP-agent credentials are scoped to least privilege. Missing for 10: documented scoping of admin/agent tokens (service accounts or PATs tied to custom roles), guidance on issuing credentials to the MCP agent, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Backend tokens are scoped to one or more projects and a single environment.
Unleash uses API keys to facilitate communication between consuming clients such as SDKs, Unleash Edge, or other tools and automation.
Enterprise users can create their own custom root roles and custom project roles.
